title: Секретный салат для постоянного гостя  (The Secret Salad for a Regular Guest)

segments.t: Listening to the cooks' stories, Max refuses to believe that mild-mannered sous-chef Lyova ever committed a serious blunder. Overhearing them, Chef Barinov laughs and recounts the story of an elderly regular guest who always ordered a special warm seafood salad that only Viktor Petrovich was allowed to prepare.
И что, он после этого тебя оставил?
Да, сказал, что я мужик.
Лев, а ты что, тоже лажал?
Да ладно, никогда не поверю.
Да ладно, никогда?
Тебе напомнить?
Уважаемый, принеси-ка мне коньяка.
А вам какого?
Самого дорогого.
Был у меня один постоянный гость.
И этому постоянному гостю готовил только я.
Теплый салат с морепродуктами.
Ну, например, я болел.
Right, let's take their exchange slowly and unpack the Russian.
И что, он после этого тебя оставил?
'And what, he kept you on the job after that?' Notice how Russian expresses 'both' and 'would keep' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Да, сказал, что я мужик.
'Yes, he said I had guts.' Lyova brings out the contrast between 'yes' and 'to say' in a few short words.
Лев, а ты что, тоже лажал?
'Lyova, did you really screw up too?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'Lev' and finishing on 'to mess up'. Lyova answers right away.
Да ладно, никогда не поверю.
'No way, I will never believe that.' In Russian, the idea of 'yes' flows naturally into 'to believe' without extra filler words.
Да ладно, никогда?
'Oh really, never?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'yes' before landing on 'never'.
Тебе напомнить?
'Should I remind you?' The grammar packs 'you' and 'reminded' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Chef Viktor answers right away.
Уважаемый, принеси-ка мне коньяка.
'My good man, bring me some cognac.' The meaning hinges on 'respected' working together with 'cognac' in spoken Russian.
А вам какого?
'Which one would you like?' In Russian, the idea of 'and' flows naturally into 'what a' without extra filler words.
Самого дорогого.
'The most expensive one.' Chef Viktor anchors the line on 'the very', while 'expensive' completes the thought. Lyova answers right away.
Был у меня один постоянный гость.
'I used to have a certain regular guest.' Lyova brings out the contrast between 'there was' and 'by' in a few short words.
И этому постоянному гостю готовил только я.
'And I was the only one who cooked for that regular guest.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'both' and 'this' in a few short words.
Теплый салат с морепродуктами.
'A warm seafood salad.' The grammar packs 'warm' and 'seafood' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Chef Viktor answers right away.
Ну, например, я болел.

'Well, one day, for instance, I was out sick.' In Russian, the idea of 'come on' flows naturally into 'to be ill' without extra filler words. Now let's listen to the entire scene again without interruption.
